attack: A2 — values crafted to miss every regex/parser, in columns with no name rule: a full name in `label`; an obfuscated email (`grace.hopper at navy dot example dot com`) in `handle2`; a phone spelled in words in `contact`; a UK National Insurance number with interleaved spaces and spelled digits (`AB nine eight seven six five four D`) in `ident`; a payment card with `.` separators in `pan`; a wordy address in `whereabouts`.
reproduction:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0
./run.sh a2 a2_values.sql
PGPASSWORD=pw psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 55432 -U ls -d tgt_a2 -x -c "select ident from records order by id limit 3"
./check.sh a2 'AB nine eight seven six five four D' 'QQ one two three four five six C' 'Grace Hopper' 'grace.hopper' '4539.1488' 'Rowan House' 'oh seven seven oh oh'
fix:
LEAKED. Exit 0. Five of the six columns were caught (label and whereabouts by the neighbouring-column rule, handle2 by the AT/DOT candidates, contact as free_text, pan by the widened Luhn separator set), but `records.ident` was reported as `no name or value signal` and crossed verbatim — 60 hits each for 'AB nine eight seven six five four D' and 'QQ one two three four five six C' in the target dump.

Root cause (verified, not guessed). textsig.ValidNationalID is correct and does recognise the attack value — a scratch copy of internal/textsig at /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0/probe returns natid=true for 'AB nine eight seven six five four D' via the candidate 'AB987654D'. The problem is that nothing on the row path ever calls it. `grep -rn ValidNationalID . --include='*.go' | grep -v _test` returns only internal/verify/catalog.go:380 and internal/plan/ddlliteral.go:109 — the two DDL-literal passes. Neither row-scanning net registers it:
  - internal/classify/classify.go:296-334, the ordered `validators` list, has entries for CatEmail, CatFinancial, CatPhone, CatNetworkID, CatOnlineID, CatCredential, CatPersonName, CatAddress — and no CatNationalID. So national_id is a NAME-ONLY category on the row path.
  - internal/verify/validators.go:133-165, the second net's table, has no CatNationalID entry either.
THREAT_MODEL.md T1's 2026-09-15 amendment (line 47) says ValidNationalID 'join[s] the strong set used by both the plan-time and the catalog pass' — both of those are DDL passes. The row path was never wired, so this is a miss-twice of exactly the shape that row's own amendment describes.

Fix, two lines plus a test:
1. internal/classify/classify.go, in the `validators` list, above the CatCredential entry:
   {pipeline.CatNationalID, phraseNationalID, true, func(_ *textsig.Dict, s string) bool { return textsig.ValidNationalID(s) }},
   with a new phraseNationalID template in internal/classify/reasons.go.
2. internal/verify/validators.go, beside the email/phone entries:
   {category: pipeline.CatNationalID, name: "national_id", text: true, strong: true, ok: textsig.ValidNationalID},
Both are safe as `strong`: I probed ValidNationalID over 22 ordinary values (pagila film titles, SKUs, timestamps, UUIDs, 'ORD-2024-0001', 'INV-99-88-77', ratings, locales) and it hit only the three real national-ID formats and correctly rejected the invalid NI prefix 'QQ123456C'. It is a strict parse with the issuing authority's exclusions, the same class of signal as email and Luhn.
3. The missing control is a parity test. internal/classify/classify.go:304-306 says of its `strong` field 'See internal/verify/validators.go's own strong field, which this mirrors validator for validator; keep the two in step' — and no test enforces it (`grep -rn 'in step\|mirrors\|parity' internal/classify/*_test.go internal/verify/*_test.go` is empty). Add a test that walks both tables and asserts the same (category, validator) set, so the next category added to one cannot silently miss the other. This is the same drift T-0055 and T-0122 already recorded twice.
The downstream path already exists: mask/register.go:55 registers MaskerNationalID for CatNationalID, and A1 proves it masks (pesel → 135896019), so this routes to a working masker rather than needing new masking code.

attack: A6 — the A2 finding reduced to its minimum and made realistic: PLAIN, unobfuscated national identifiers in columns whose names miss the rule pack, in a table with no other personal column so the neighbouring-column rule cannot fire. `ref_code` holds hyphenated US SSNs (078-05-NNNN); `ni_ref` holds UK NI numbers (ABNNNNNND).
reproduction:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0
./run.sh a6 a6_natid.sql
PGPASSWORD=pw psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 55432 -U ls -d tgt_a6 -c 'select id,ref_code,ni_ref from benefit_claims order by id limit 5'
./check.sh a6 '078-05-' 'AB100' 'AB1000'
fix:
LEAKED, and this is the severe form of the A2 finding — no obfuscation is required at all. Exit 0. Both columns reported `no name or value signal`. All 300 rows crossed verbatim: target rows read `1 | 078-05-1001 | AB100001D`, and the dump greps at 300 hits for '078-05-' and 300 for 'AB100'.

This is the same single root cause as A2 (national_id has no value validator on either row net — see the A2 fix for the exact code sites and the two-line change). What A6 adds is the severity argument: the previous round framed the national-ID miss as an obfuscated-value problem and fixed it inside textsig.spelledDigits, but the value never needed obfuscating. A column called `ni_ref` — a name a real payroll or benefits schema would plausibly use — holding textbook-format national identifiers is copied to the target under a green tick, with the report affirmatively printing 'no name or value signal', which reads as a clean bill of health for a column nothing looked inside.

Alongside the two-line fix, THREAT_MODEL.md T1 needs amending: its 2026-09-15 text implies ValidNationalID is a live control, and on the row path it is not.

attack: A7 — the same national_id gap reached through two other carriers: a `text[]` of UK NI numbers (`id_list`), a plain SSN in a column called `code`, and a JSON document in a `text` column whose only personal datum is an SSN at depth 3 (`doc`).
reproduction:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0
./run.sh a7 a7_natid_nested.sql
PGPASSWORD=pw psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 55432 -U ls -d tgt_a7 -x -c 'select doc,id_list,code from audit_docs order by id limit 2'
./check.sh a7 '078-05-' 'AB100' 'JG200' '123-45-'
fix:
LEAKED, twice, same root cause as A2/A6. Exit 0.
  - `id_list` (text[] of NI numbers): 300 hits each for 'AB100' and 'JG200'; target holds `{AB100001D,JG200001A}`. The array machinery correctly split the elements and offered each to the validators — there is simply no national_id validator to hit.
  - `code` (plain SSN, column literally named `code`): 300 hits for '123-45-'.
  - `doc` was NOT leaked, but only by accident: the compact JSON string tripped textsig.LooksSecret's entropy guess (`200/200 samples look like secrets`) and was masked to the fixed credential literal `$lazyslice$invalid`. That is luck, not a control — and it also destroys the JSON structure, so a developer gets an unparseable document.
The fix is the A2 fix; no separate change. Worth noting for the fix's test coverage that the array path and the scalar path both need a regression case, since they reach the validator through different code (scalarsOf's array branch vs. the plain scalar branch).

attack: A9b — A9 with the Luhn-valid card removed, so the second net's only numeric-family entry cannot fire. All that remains is an SSN stored as `bigint` (`taxref`) and a phone stored as `numeric` (`msisdn`).
reproduction:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-0
./run.sh a9b a9b_numeric.sql
PGPASSWORD=pw psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 55432 -U ls -d tgt_a9b -c 'select id,taxref,msisdn from payroll order by id limit 4'
./check.sh a9b '78051' '44770090'
fix:
LEAKED. Exit 0. `msisdn` was saved by its name matching phone and was masked to a fake number, but `taxref` was reported `no name or value signal` and all 300 SSNs crossed verbatim (300 hits for '78051'; target shows `1 | 78051001`).

This is a RELATED BUT DISTINCT gap from A2/A6/A7, and the A2 two-line fix does NOT close it. Two separate reasons, both verified in the probe:
  1. textsig.ValidNationalID requires the separators. Probed: '123-45-1001' → true, but '123451001', '078051001' and '78051001' → all false. There is no separator-free 9-digit SSN spelling, so even a registered validator would not see a numeric column's rendered value. (A numeric column also silently loses the leading zero, so 078-05-1001 renders as the 8-digit '78051001'.)
  2. ADR-010's recall boundary silences value signals on the numeric family for categories whose maskers emit text — and national_id is currently treated as one of those.

Fix, in three parts:
  a. Exempt national_id from the ADR-010 numeric silencing. This is justified by code that already exists: mask/corpus_test.go:46 is a case named 'national id bigint' masking '78051120', and mask/canonical.go:131 handles CatNationalID alongside CatFinancial for the number tag — MaskerNationalID already emits digits for numeric families, so the premise of the silencing ('maskers emit text') is false for this category.
  b. Give the second net a `digits: true`, non-strong, ratio-scored national_id entry, exactly mirroring the Luhn split at internal/verify/validators.go:158 and for the same reason: an unseparated 9-digit run is a weak claim, so it must be ratio-scored rather than strong, or ordinary bigint id columns would fail every run with no green path.
  c. Add a zero-padded, separator-free SSN spelling to textsig.Candidates (pad a rendered 8-digit numeric back to 9) rather than loosening validNationalID's pattern, so the precision of the strong text-side entry recommended in the A2 fix is untouched. Keep that spelling out of the strong DDL-literal set.
Since this changes what is masked, it is a THREAT_MODEL.md T1 question and needs the T1 review the classify CLAUDE.md demands, not just a test pass.

attack: A10 — the residual THREAT_MODEL.md T1 states but does not close: a person's full name the dictionary does not carry, in a column called `label` whose name matches no rule, in a table with no other personal column. Khmer, Lao and Amharic transliterations (Sokhem Chanthavy, Bounmy Phimmasone, Tesfaye Gebreselassie, Rithy Sopheak, Khamla Vongsa).
fix:
LEAKED — 60 hits for each of the five names, exit 0, column reported `no name or value signal`.

This is the acknowledged residual, stated almost verbatim in THREAT_MODEL.md T1 line 41 ('a name in a language the dictionary does not carry, in a column named in that language, with no other signal in the table') and line 50 ('the value validators are a net over recognised shapes only'). I report it because it reproduced cleanly and because the report line is actively misleading, not because the class is new.

I do not think widening names.txt is the fix — the class is unbounded, and the file's own precision rules (nothing under three characters, no ordinary English words) are what keep it usable. Two things that would help without pretending the class is closed:
  1. Change the reason string. `no name or value signal` reads as a finding of absence. For a character column that was looked at and matched nothing, say so as an absence of evidence — e.g. 'nothing recognised; not proof the column is impersonal' — so the transcript stops implying a clean bill of health. This is cheap and it is the honest half.
  2. Extend the unknownColumnsBesideCertain rail. It currently fires only in a table that already holds a `certain` person-identifying column, which is exactly the table A10 does not have. A table whose ONLY unexplained column is a short free-text column with no unique index and no type conflict is the shape worth a `possible`, or at minimum a printed prompt in interactive mode. That is an ADR-level recall/precision trade, not a patch — it should go to the tracker rather than be slipped in.
File as a tracker item under the T1 residual rather than treating it as a regression.

attack: Wrong target, alias: defeat ARCHITECTURE.md §9 rule 1 by reaching one production cluster over two transports. sqlClusterID (internal/pg/source.go:299) is pg_postmaster_start_time() || host(inet_server_addr()) || inet_server_port(). inet_server_addr()/inet_server_port() are NULL on a Unix-socket connection, so the SAME cluster reports two different 'cluster identities' depending on how you dialled it. The SELECT-only source role ARCHITECTURE.md §9 recommends cannot EXECUTE pg_control_system(), so system_identifier is "" on the source side and the whole of rule 1 falls to this transport-dependent value. Target: an empty production database (the mid-migration case) on the source's own cluster, named over the socket.
reproduction:
# lab (all scratch under /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-1/r2, referred to as $B)
B=/private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-1/r2; mkdir -p $B/sock
/opt/homebrew/bin/initdb -D $B/pgdata -U postgres --auth=trust
/opt/homebrew/bin/pg_ctl -D $B/pgdata -o "-p 15600 -h 127.0.0.1 -k $B/sock" -l $B/pg.log start
/opt/homebrew/bin/psql postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/postgres -f $B/prod.sql
#   prod.sql: db app with customers(email,full_name,phone,ssn)+orders (50/200 real rows);
#   CREATE ROLE reader LOGIN PASSWORD 'pw' with SELECT only;
#   REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_control_system() FROM public;
#   db newprod = the same two tables, EMPTY (a freshly provisioned production database)

# the two identities of one cluster
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/app -c "select pg_postmaster_start_time()::text||'|'||coalesce(host(inet_server_addr()),'')||'|'||coalesce(inet_server_port()::text,'')"
#  -> 2026-09-15 01:54:11.534898-04|127.0.0.1|15600
psql -tA "postgres://postgres@/app?host=$B/sock&port=15600" -c "<same>"
#  -> 2026-09-15 01:54:11.534898-04||          <-- same server, different identity

export LAZYSLICE_SECRET=$(openssl rand -hex 32)
go build -o $B/lazyslice ./cmd/lazyslice

# CONTROL, TCP target on the same cluster - the warning fires:
$B/lazyslice --source 'postgres://reader:pw@127.0.0.1:15600/app' \
  --target 'postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod' --yes --no-config -n 5
#  ! target newprod is on the same cluster as the source: this run writes to the source's own server

# ATTACK, same cluster, same database, spelled as the socket:
$B/lazyslice --source 'postgres://reader:pw@127.0.0.1:15600/app' \
  --target "postgres://postgres@/newprod?host=$B/sock&port=15600" --yes --no-config -n 5; echo exit=$?
#  target newprod on /private/.../sock - --target
#  dropping public.orders in the target
#  dropping public.customers in the target
#  public.customers: 5 rows / public.orders: 20 rows
#  exit=0, and NOT ONE same-cluster line (grep -c 'same cluster' -> 0)
psql -tA postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:15600/newprod -c 'select count(*) from customers'  # -> 5
fix: Two changes in internal/pg. (1) sqlClusterID must not be computed from anything that varies with the transport or the client's spelling. inet_server_addr()/inet_server_port() are properties of the *connection*, not of the cluster; replace them with values that are the same for every session on the postmaster and readable by PUBLIC: `SELECT pg_postmaster_start_time()::text || '|' || current_setting('port')`. Both are transport-independent (current_setting('port') is the server's own listen port, and is the value a socket connection reports too), and a false *match* between two genuinely different clusters is the fail-safe direction here (an over-refusal), whereas a false mismatch is the production write this attempt performed. Add internal/pg/lease_integration_test.go-style coverage that asserts ClusterID() over a Unix socket equals ClusterID() over TCP against one container - that single assertion is what this whole finding reduces to. (2) Harden the fail-closed arm in Target.Gate: clusterUnknown() currently returns false as soon as both sides produced a non-empty cluster identity, so a *mismatch* produced by transport is read as positive evidence of two different servers. Rule 1 should treat 'the two identities differ but neither side could be corroborated by system_identifier' as unknown rather than as proof, i.e. the sameCatalog arm should fire on `currentDB == source.Database` whenever system_identifier is unavailable on either side, regardless of what the weaker cluster identity said. (3) Independently: ARCHITECTURE.md §9's recommended-role snippet (printed verbatim by the run header, internal/core/run.go's CodeRoleWritable message) should append `GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION pg_control_system() TO lazyslice_ro;` so the one identity that actually survives aliasing is readable by the role the tool tells operators to create. Every attack in this report that turned on 'the recommended role cannot read system_identifier' is closed by that one line.

attack: Catalog residue via table CHECK constraints carrying non-"strong" personal data (person name, postal address, special-category sentence). internal/verify/catalog.go's strongCatalogHit and internal/plan/ddlliteral.go's strongHit both run only five validators (email, phone, Luhn, IBAN, national_id), so every other category the pipeline masks in rows — person_name, address, free_text, special_category, geo, online_id, network_id, credential — passes through the DDL boundary untouched.
reproduction:
Containers: docker run -d --name rt2-src -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=srcpw -e POSTGRES_USER=srcuser -e POSTGRES_DB=srcdb -p 55531:5432 postgres:16 ; docker run -d --name rt2-tgt -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=tgtpw -e POSTGRES_USER=tgtuser -e POSTGRES_DB=tgtdb -p 55532:5432 postgres:16
Binary: cd /Users/gareth/personal_repos/lazyslice && go build -o /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/lazyslice ./cmd/lazyslice
Schema: /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/schema1.sql — docker exec -i rt2-src psql -U srcuser -d srcdb -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 < /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/schema1.sql
  CONSTRAINT ck_name_block  CHECK (full_name <> 'Aurelio Nakamura-Okonkwo')
  CONSTRAINT ck_addr_block  CHECK (street_address IS NULL OR street_address <> '1742 Kestrel Hollow Lane, Ashford VT 05024')
  CONSTRAINT ck_notes_free  CHECK (notes IS NULL OR notes <> 'Priya Raghunathan disclosed her HIV diagnosis on 2019-04-02')
Run: cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/run1 && /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/lazyslice --source 'postgres://srcuser:srcpw@127.0.0.1:55531/srcdb?sslmode=disable' --target 'postgres://tgtuser:tgtpw@127.0.0.1:55532/tgtdb?sslmode=disable' --root public.customers --take 10 --yes
Read back: docker exec rt2-tgt psql -U tgtuser -d tgtdb -At -c "SELECT conname, pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE contype='c' AND conrelid<>0;"
fix: The five strong validators are the wrong boundary for a CHECK. They were chosen (internal/verify/catalog.go's own comment) because dictionary-backed validators would false-positive on a column named after a street — but that reasoning applies to *identifiers* in the expression, not to its *string literals*, which are the only thing pipeline.Literals returns. Run the full nine-validator second net (internal/verify/secondnet.go) over literals only, not over the whole expression text, in both internal/plan/ddlliteral.go strongHit and internal/verify/catalog.go strongCatalogHit. Where a validator is genuinely too noisy for a literal, fail towards the operator rather than towards silence: a run that recreates a CHECK, an index predicate, a generated expression, an enum label or a domain default containing any non-empty, non-pattern string literal on a column the run classified as personal should print that literal's object at warn level and require --allow-type-literal (or a new --allow-ddl-literal) to proceed. Refusing loudly is what exit 13 already does for email; the fix is to stop the category list from being shorter than the list of categories the row pipeline masks.

attack: Catalog residue via partial index predicates. internal/plan reads no pg_index at all (tracker T-0163) and internal/verify's catalog pass only applies the five strong validators, so `CREATE INDEX ... WHERE <col> = '<name or address>'` is replayed verbatim into the target by internal/load/ddl's pg_get_indexdef path and nothing looks at it.
fix: Two halves. (a) Close T-0163 so internal/plan reads pg_index and refuses or rewrites before anything is dropped, rather than leaving the index predicate as the one route only the post-load catalog pass walks — a refusal after the load means the target already held the value for the length of the run. (b) Apply the widened validator set from attempt 1's fix to the pg_index arm of internal/verify/catalog.go. An index predicate is never rewritten (the catalog.go comment says so), so any hit in one is by construction the source's own literal and can be an unconditional refusal.

attack: Catalog residue via the four object kinds the 2026-09-15 A4b/A11/A12 amendment added — enum labels, domain CHECK, domain DEFAULT, generated-column expressions — using a non-strong category. The amendment added the *reads*; it did not widen the *validators*, so the same objects that now refuse an email in a label carry a person's name, a postal address or a health disclosure straight through.
fix: Same single fix as attempt 1 — these four reads already exist and already funnel through strongCatalogHit/strongHit, so widening those two functions closes all four at once. Worth recording in THREAT_MODEL.md T1 explicitly: the amendment's sentence 'Every string literal in each text goes through the strong validators' is the whole of the gap, and the list of categories the DDL boundary recognises must be kept equal to the list the row boundary masks, not a subset of it.

attack: Bypass the strong-validator net for a genuinely strong category by putting the value on the right-hand side of a pattern operator. pipeline.Literal.Pattern (internal/pipeline/ddlliteral.go afterPatternOperator) marks any literal after LIKE/ILIKE/SIMILAR TO/~/~*/!~/!~* as a shape and never a value, and both strongHit and strongCatalogHit return "" unconditionally for it. A regex that IS the address is a value.
reproduction:
Contained in schema1.sql: CONSTRAINT ck_email_regex CHECK (email !~ '^ceo@bigcorp\.example$')
Control, to show the non-pattern form is caught: docker exec rt2-src psql -U srcuser -d srcdb -q -c "ALTER TABLE customers ADD CONSTRAINT ck_email_plain CHECK (email <> 'ceo@bigcorp.example');" then the same run -> exit 13, 'target.schema.literal_not_rewritable'. Drop it again and rerun -> exit 0.
Read back: docker exec rt2-tgt psql -U tgtuser -d tgtdb -At -c "SELECT pg_get_constraintdef(oid) FROM pg_constraint WHERE conname='ck_email_regex';"
-> CHECK ((email !~ '^ceo@bigcorp\.example$'::text)) — the real address is in the target, exit 0, while the semantically identical `<>` form is exit 13.
fix: The Pattern exemption is correct in its motivating case ('%@%.%' is a shape) and wrong in general. Do not exempt a pattern literal from *detection*; exempt it from *rewriting* only — which internal/pipeline/ddlliteral.go already does independently via Rewritable. Concretely: in internal/plan/ddlliteral.go strongHit and internal/verify/catalog.go strongCatalogHit, stop returning "" for lit.Pattern; instead strip regex/LIKE metacharacters and anchors (^ $ % _ \ . * + ? [ ] ( ) { } |) from the literal, and run the validators on what is left. '%@%.%' reduces to '@' and matches nothing; '^ceo@bigcorp\.example$' reduces to 'ceo@bigcorp.example' and is exit 13, which is the right answer. Keep the testdata/nasty.sql LIKE case as the regression test for the stripping, since it is what the current blanket exemption was written for (T-0134).

attack: A custom masker that returns its input verbatim (THREAT_MODEL.md T12 / tracker T-0180), registered against the public mask module.
reproduction:
Scratch module: /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/maskprobe (go.mod replaces github.com/Liarea/lazyslice/mask with the repo's mask/ directory).
type passthrough struct{}; func (passthrough) Mask(h [32]byte, in mask.Value, c mask.Constraints) (mask.Value, error) { return in, nil }
mask.Register("rt2_passthrough", mask.CatEmail, passthrough{})
r, err := mask.Apply(k, mask.CatEmail, "rt2_passthrough", mask.Value{Text: "victim.canary@bigcorp.example"}, mask.Constraints{TypeTag: "text"})
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/maskprobe && go run .
-> PASSTHROUGH: out="victim.canary@bigcorp.example" masked=true err=<nil>
fix: Already carried as tracker T-0180 and already correctly scoped in the THREAT_MODEL.md T12 amendment: the post-condition belongs inside mask.Apply and must exempt the two paths that are meant to return the input (a masked enum emitting a member label, a collapsed special_category emitting the first member), so it is a category/constraints-aware check and not a bare `out == in`. Concretely, in mask/mask.go Apply, after m.Mask: when c.EnumLabels is empty and the category is not a collapsed special_category, compare the canonical form of out against canon and return a new ErrPassthrough naming the masker id and the category only. Confirming it is still open, and that the residual scan remains the only thing between a passthrough generator and a shipped cleartext column.

attack: A custom masker that panics halfway with the value in its panic message (T7's central case; tracker T-0181).
reproduction:
Same maskprobe module: func (panicker) Mask(...) { panic(fmt.Sprintf("masker blew up halfway on %q", in.Text)) } ; mask.Register("rt2_panic", mask.CatEmail, panicker{}) ; mask.Apply(...)
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/maskprobe && go run .
-> PANIC ESCAPED Apply: masker blew up halfway on "victim.canary@bigcorp.example"
fix: Open as tracker T-0181, and the module-level leak is real: mask.Apply does not recover, so the panic value crosses the module boundary with the row value in it. The CLI half is genuinely fixed — cmd/lazyslice/main.go reportPanic and internal/core's panicError both route through core.PanicSummary, which prints 'a value of type string (it is withheld...)' — so a lazyslice run no longer prints it. But mask/ is a public module anyone can import (ADR-006's whole point), and its own contract should not depend on the parent binary's redaction. Add the recover in mask.Apply, converting the panic into an error that names the masker id and the category and nothing else.

attack: A custom masker that RETURNS (rather than panics with) an error quoting the value it could not mask. This is the same free-form-string egress the 2026-09-15 panic amendment closed, through the one door the amendment did not check.
reproduction:
Same maskprobe module: func (erroring) Mask(...) (mask.Value, error) { return mask.Value{}, fmt.Errorf("cannot mask %q: unsupported shape", in.Text) }
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/maskprobe && go run .
-> ERROR-RETURN: err=cannot mask "victim.canary@bigcorp.example": unsupported shape
Code path to stderr, read rather than executed (no runtime masker loading exists in v1, so this is not reproducible through the CLI today): internal/transform/transform.go maskScalar wraps the masker error as &Refusal{..., Reason: err}; internal/transform/codes.go Refusal.Error() renders it as fmt.Sprintf("transform: masker %s refused %s: %v", ..., r.Reason); cmd/lazyslice/main.go report() -> renderSafe(err, showValues), which scrubs only *pgconn.PgError and panic-carrying errors and otherwise returns err.Error() verbatim, with no flag required.
fix: Close the asymmetry: a masker's message is withheld when it arrives as a panic and printed when it arrives as an error, and the two are the same string. (a) In internal/transform/codes.go, stop interpolating r.Reason into Refusal.Error(); the doc comment there already promises 'It never carries the value that could not be masked', and today only the *event* keeps that promise while Error() breaks it. Render the reason only under --show-row-values-in-errors, exactly as PanicSummary does, and otherwise print the reason's type. (b) In cmd/lazyslice/main.go renderSafe, make redaction the default rather than the exception: errors that are known value-free (core.Stop with a catalogue code, errUsage, pipeline.ErrNotImplemented) print in full; everything else prints its type plus the --show-row-values-in-errors hint. The current shape — an allowlist of two error types to scrub, and `return err.Error()` for everything else — means every new error type in the tree is value-bearing until someone notices. Note also that built-in error messages are clean today (I grepped internal/ and mask/ for value-bearing formats and found none), so this is a contract fix, not a live CLI leak.

attack: Take the masking key out of the repository through a symlinked PARENT DIRECTORY, defeating the A15 fix. internal/core/run.go line 1942 does os.Lstat on r.req.SecretFile itself, which checks only the final path component; a symlinked directory component is not seen, and repo.Protect then writes a .gitignore entry for a path that holds nothing.
reproduction:
mkdir -p /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/sym/repo /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/sym/Dropbox
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/sym/repo && git init -q . && printf 'x\n' > .gitignore && ln -s ../Dropbox cloudkeys
.../lazyslice --source 'postgres://srcuser:srcpw@127.0.0.1:55531/srcdb?sslmode=disable' --target 'postgres://tgtuser:tgtpw@127.0.0.1:55532/tgtdb?sslmode=disable' --root public.customers --take 10 --yes --secret-file ./cloudkeys/lazyslice.secret
Exit 0. Transcript says: 'added /cloudkeys/lazyslice.secret to .gitignore' and 'wrote a new masking key to ./cloudkeys/lazyslice.secret'.
ls -la ../Dropbox -> -rw------- lazyslice.secret, 65 bytes, outside the repository, in the cloud-synced folder.
cat .gitignore -> contains '/cloudkeys/lazyslice.secret', which protects a path that is a symlink and no file.
fix: Resolve the whole path, not the last component, before deciding anything. In internal/core/run.go's secret-file check, replace the single os.Lstat with filepath.EvalSymlinks on the parent directory (or walk each component with os.Lstat): if the resolved absolute path differs from the given one, apply the same secret.refused.symlink exit 5. The threat model's carve-out — '--secret-file pointing straight at a file outside the repository is unaffected, that is an operator naming a location' — does not cover this case and should be narrowed to say so: here the operator named an in-repository location, was given the in-repository treatment (a .gitignore line and a printed reassurance), and the key landed outside. The rule that makes both cases right is: the .gitignore entry and the tracked-file check must be applied to the *resolved* path, and a resolved path outside the repository must print 'unprotected' rather than 'added to .gitignore'.

attack: Take the masking key out of the repository through a HARD link, which no path-based check can see.
reproduction:
mkdir -p /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/hard/repo /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/hard/Dropbox
cd .../hard/repo && git init -q . && printf 'x\n' > .gitignore
.../lazyslice --source ... --target ... --root public.customers --take 10 --yes     # creates ./lazyslice.secret 0600, exit 0
ln lazyslice.secret ../Dropbox/leaked.key
.../lazyslice --source ... --target ... --root public.customers --take 10 --yes     # exit 0, says nothing about the key
diff lazyslice.secret ../Dropbox/leaked.key -> identical; ls -la ../Dropbox shows link count 2.
fix: Lower severity than the symlink case — it needs write access to the repository directory — but it is the same promise ('the key is protected by .gitignore') failing silently, and it is cheap to detect. When reading or creating the secret file, stat it and refuse (or at minimum warn loudly, in the same shape as secret.refused.permissive) when Sys().(*syscall.Stat_t).Nlink > 1: a key file with more than one name is reachable under a name the repository rule never saw. Pair it with the existing mode check in the same function so the two 'this key may already have been read' conditions are reported together.

attack: Get a password into the committed lazyslice.yml through --password-command, which THREAT_MODEL.md T5 records as being stored 'as the command string'.
reproduction:
cd /private/tmp/claude-501/lazyslice-scratch/redteam-2/run8 && .../lazyslice --source 'postgres://srcuser:srcpw@127.0.0.1:55531/srcdb?sslmode=disable' --target 'postgres://tgtuser:tgtpw@127.0.0.1:55532/tgtdb?sslmode=disable' --root public.customers --take 10 --yes --password-command 'vault read -field=pw secret/db # Hunter2InCommand'
exit 0; grep -n password_command lazyslice.yml ->
  password_command: "vault read -field=pw secret/db # Hunter2InCommand"
Second, separate problem found while reproducing this: the flag is never executed. grep -rn 'exec.Command' over internal/ and cmd/ returns exactly one hit, internal/repo/repo.go:301 (git ls-files), and nothing in internal/discover or internal/dsn reads core.Request.PasswordCommand — it is plumbed only as far as internal/emit. A run that relies on it fails authentication:
  .../lazyslice --source 'postgres://srcuser@127.0.0.1:55531/srcdb?sslmode=disable' --target ... --yes --password-command 'printf srcpw'
  -> exit 3, 'lazyslice: password authentication failed for user "srcuser" (SQLSTATE 28P01)'
fix: Two things. (a) The command string is a documented place for a secret to appear and it is written into the file whose header says 'This file never contains a secret' — make that true: run the emitted password_command through a heuristic before writing it (reject/withhold when the command's argv contains a literal that is not a path, an env reference, or a known credential-helper subcommand; echo/printf/cat with a literal argument being the obvious case), record password_command_fingerprint the way --where already records where_fingerprint, and print that it was withheld. At minimum, warn at write time when the command is echo/printf/cat with a literal. (b) --password-command is advertised in --help and in the post-prompt remedy text, is accepted, is recorded into the committed config, and does nothing — so an operator who follows the tool's own advice gets an auth failure and falls back to putting the password in the DSN or in PGPASSWORD, which is the outcome the flag exists to prevent. Either implement it in internal/discover (exec the command, trim one trailing newline, never log stdout) or make it exit 2 as unimplemented in this build. Shipping it as a no-op that still writes itself into the yml is the worst of the three.
